discovery_close_gate: ARMED — discovery closes after V4C-4 regardless of result

sources.description: US CPI All Urban Consumers (BLS release, FRED CPIAUCSL)
sources.revision_scope: CPI is revised within the release cycle: preliminary, then final. YoY figures can be restated when seasonal factors are updated annually (Jan). Typical magnitude: ±0.1 pp YoY in seasonal revisions.
sources.consensus_vintage_note: Consensus polls are collected by Bloomberg/Reuters from professional forecasters in the days before each release. Historical poll vintage data (what was the consensus as-of T-1 day before release N) is not publicly available. Current-database consensus reflects the final polled value, not the real-time pre-release snapshot used by traders.

sources.description: US Nonfarm Payrolls (BLS Employment Situation, FRED PAYEMS)
sources.revision_scope: NFP is subject to two subsequent monthly revisions (preliminary, second estimate). Annual benchmark revisions occur in Feb. Typical preliminary-to-final revision: ±50k–100k jobs (0.03–0.07% of employment). The benchmark revision (2024) revised 2023 figures by ~800k jobs.
sources.consensus_vintage_note: Same provenance boundary as CPI. Bloomberg consensus polls are not free. In addition, the 2024 benchmark revision retroactively changed 2023 headline figures by ~818k jobs — if a model is trained with post-revision data, it has implicit lookahead on the exact series value a model would have seen at trade time.

sources.description: FOMC rate decisions (Federal Reserve press releases)
sources.revision_scope: Rate decision (hike/hold/cut) is not revised — it is the official policy action. Statement text is the official record. Dot plot and projections released quarterly may be revised in subsequent meetings but are not retroactively restated.
sources.consensus_vintage_note: Rate-change surprise = actual_rate_change − market_implied_expectation. Market-implied expectation (from OIS or Fed funds futures) must be snapshotted just before the 2 PM ET announcement. Historical snapshots of OIS-implied probability distributions are not freely available; they require Bloomberg WIRP function historical data or similar proprietary feed. Binary direction (hike/hold/cut) IS PIT-safe from Fed press releases alone.

special_findings.description: The 2024 annual benchmark revision retroactively revised 2023 NFP figures by approximately −818k jobs. Any model trained or evaluated with post-revision PAYEMS data for the 2023 period has implicit lookahead. FRED vintage API (REALTIME_START parameter) is required to obtain first-print values — this requires an API key not present in this environment. Gate C3 for NFP must be classified MAJOR_REVISION_RISK until vintage-correct data can be confirmed.

The surprise feature (actual - consensus) is the primary information vector for macro event strategies. It fails universally because historical consensus snapshots require Bloomberg BEST function or Reuters terminal data. This is a structural, not incidental, provenance boundary.

overall_note: All three macro event sources fail C7 (surprise PIT safety) because Bloomberg/Reuters consensus vintage data is not publicly available. The feature family `surprise = actual - consensus` cannot be constructed with PIT safety from free data sources. Binary event-state features (hike/hold/cut, above/below consensus direction) are PIT-safe from release dates alone but have lower information content.
binary_event_state_note: Binary event-state features (fomc_hike_cut_hold, cpi_above_prior_direction, nfp_headline_first_print) are PIT-safe from public release dates but are out of scope for V4C-4B given that the primary surprise feature family is rejected. If binary event-state features are to be researched, they require a new scoped audit.
